item.title: February 2026 Market Review from Hankins & Boggs Group
item.description: Markets were volatile in February, but gains in previously overlooked non-tech stocks helped keep averages flat as mega-cap momentum slowed. Tariff uncertainty continues to dominate headlines for a second year.

item.title: Cuts To State Boards And Commissions Wins Legislature’s OK
item.description: A few dozen of Indiana’s state boards and commissions face elimination as legislators on Friday, Feb. 27 endorsed a plan principally aimed at panels deemed unproductive.

item.title: Cal-Maine Foods Announces Acquisition Of Creighton Brothers LLC
item.description: Cal-Maine Foods, Inc., the largest egg company in the United States and a leading player in the egg-based food industry, recently announced the acquisition of the shell egg, egg products and prepared foods assets of Creighton Brothers LLC, including Crystal Lake LLC, for a total purchase price of approximately $128.5 million, subject to customary post-closing adjustments.

item.title: Wholesale Inflation Accelerates in January, Exceeds Forecasts
item.description: U.S. wholesale prices rose more than expected in January, underscoring persistent inflation pressures and complicating the policy outlook for the Federal Reserve.

item.title: Interra Wraps Up 32nd Hometown Giving
item.description: Interra Credit Union staff recently announced the success of their 32nd annual Hometown Giving campaign, which raised $43,577 to support more than 40 local non-profit organizations.

item.title: Indiana Senate Rejects Early Voting Reduction
item.description: Indiana lawmakers killed a proposal to shorten early in-person voting across the state.

item.description: Curt Cignetti is guaranteed more than $100 million over the life of his revised contract, per terms released by Indiana on Monday, March 2 morning.

item.title: Judge Grants Summary Judgment To Capital Chronicle In Execution Drug Costs Case
item.description: A Marion County judge on Friday, Feb. 27 resolved a public records lawsuit in favor of the Indiana Capital Chronicle, granting summary judgment and finding that corrections officials violated Indiana’s public access law by improperly withholding the information.
